_comment: Copy this file to intents.json (gitignored) and edit. The bridge matches each incoming message against every intent's regex in order; the first match runs its HTTP pipeline and returns a reply, skipping Claude entirely. Leave intents.json absent (or with an empty intents array) to disable.

_schema.name: human-readable id for logs
_schema.match: Python regex applied to the trimmed message; use named groups (?P<value>...) to capture data. The first non-None named group is exposed as {value}.
_schema.steps: Ordered list. Each step is either an HTTP call (url + method + ...) or a control step (skip_if / reply).
_schema.step.url: URL template. ${ENV_VAR} expands from .env / process env. {ctx.path} pulls from prior step output or named regex groups.
_schema.step.headers/params/json: Templated the same way as url.
_schema.step.extract: Dotted/bracketed path applied to the JSON response before saving (e.g. '[0]' takes the first array element).
_schema.step.save_as: Name to bind the (post-extract) response under in the context, e.g. 'lookup'.
_schema.step.fail_if_empty: If the extracted value is empty/None, return FAIL: with this template (rendered).
_schema.step.skip_if: Path that, if truthy, skips this step. With skip_reply, returns immediately instead of skipping.
_schema.step.skip_reply: Reply template returned when skip_if matches — short-circuits the whole pipeline.
_schema.step.reply: Pure-reply step (no url): renders this template and returns. Useful with skip_if for branching.
_schema.reply: Template returned on successful completion of all steps.

intents.name: radarr_add
intents._comment: Matches 'add X to Radarr', 'Radarr: X', 'Radarr add X', and Finnish 'lisää X radariin'. Requires RADARR_URL and RADARR_API_KEY in .env. Picks the top lookup hit + first quality profile + first root folder and triggers an immediate search.
intents.reply: OK: Added {lookup.title} ({lookup.year}) to Radarr — profile: {qp.name}, root: {rf.path}. Search triggered.

intents.name: tts_announce
intents._comment: Calls a Home Assistant script that wakes a media player, sets volume, and speaks the captured text. The script encapsulates all sequencing (turn_on + delay + volume + tts.<engine>_say) so the bridge stays generic. Requires HA_URL, HA_TOKEN, HA_TTS_SCRIPT in .env, and a matching script on the HA side that accepts a `message` field. See README for an example script.
